vertices.description: List of all vertices in this graph.

edges.description: List of all edges in this graph.

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

finallyVertex.description:
Optional link to a parent {@link FlowGraph}. This field is intended to be populated when there exists
translations between {@link FlowGraph}s and allows the execution metadata to be aggregated to the original
{@link FlowGraph}.

asyncRuns.description: Previous asynchronous executions for this workflow

title:
The {@link Workflow} is an intermediate representation language that represents a directed port graph of
steps. Each {@link Workflow.Vertex} represents a specialized step.
There are several types of vertices:
1. Action-based Vertex
   - e.g. Action, Batch, MapReduce, Export, Import
   - explicit inputs and outputs, represented by input and output ports, respectively
   - "$start" input port, whose data is typed as {@link Workflow.Signal}. This is often, but not required to be, connected
     to a "$success" output port of another vertex, indicating an implicit data relationship for e.g. non-pure functions
   - "$success" output port, whose data is typed as {@link Workflow.Signal}. This is often, but not required to be, connected
     to a "$start" input port of another vertex, indicating an implicit data relationship for e.g. non-pure functions
   - "error" output port, whose data is typed as {@link Error}. This can be used as an input to subsequent steps
     for custom error-handling
   - NOTE: the "$" prefix naming convention is used to distinguish "control" (i.e. {@link Workflow.Signal}) from traditional "data"
2. Input/Output Vertex
   - e.g. Input, Output, Const
   - represent high-level arguments and high-level return values for the workflow itself
3. Control Flow
   - e.g. Conditional

@see workflow.c3doc.md
